Acadify MVP wireframes — Sprint 04

Acadify is a responsive WEB APP, not a mobile app. Top row and the first two of the second row are the primary design target at 1280px: persistent 240px sidebar, top bar with breadcrumbs and global search, content capped at 1200px.

The four small frames are the same website at 360px — one implementation, different container.

Low fidelity on purpose: greyscale, no brand. Colour, mascot and icon set are Sprint 05; components are Sprint 06.
Width buys MORE PANELS VISIBLE AT ONCE, not wider text. Content caps at 1200px so reading lines stay 60–75 characters — a 4K monitor gets margin, not 300-character paragraphs.

Reviewer plus a scoped Ask panel — the layout only a browser window can give you. Read and interrogate at once, with page citations on every section. Below 1024px the panel becomes its own route and the scope carries over.
The score is not the point — the next action is. Wrong answers open by default, correct ones collapse, and 'ask why I got this wrong' is the highest-value link in the app.

Focus mode drops all nav chrome and caps at 720px at EVERY width, so an exam-like screen feels identical on a laptop and a phone. Keyboard shortcuts (1–4, arrows) because a laptop student should not need the mouse mid-quiz.

No bottom tab bar. Bottom tabs are native-app chrome; on a website they read as an imitation app and fight the browser's own bottom bar and the on-screen keyboard. The sidebar becomes a drawer behind the ☰ instead, and each screen's primary action stays in the content column within thumb reach.
